key_facts: YouTube Data API v3 captions.download REQUIRES OAuth + video ownership — USELESS for this project (users watch OTHER people's videos)
yt-dlp is the ONLY reliable subtitle extraction approach — no API key, TypeScript wrappers exist, extracts VTT from any public video
Modular monolith (NestJS modules) is the right architecture — greenfield, small team, extract to microservices later if needed
Subtitle sync via polling getCurrentTime() at 100ms — YouTube IFrame API has no caption-change event
Aggressive per-video-ID caching — subtitles never change, cache once serve forever
AnkiConnect runs on localhost:8765 — backend bridges the connection, not frontend
Auth is DEFERRED — Feature #1 doesn't need it, add when multi-user features arrive
call_chains: Frontend POST /api/videos {url} -> video.module -> subtitle.module -> yt-dlp child process -> VTT parse -> Drizzle -> Postgres
Frontend polls getCurrentTime() -> match to subtitle_segments -> render active line
Word click -> translation.module -> cache lookup or external API -> return translation
blast_radius: Entire project is greenfield — no existing files to break
